<subject>Fw: Summary of Meeting on Warehouse Space Reallocation</subject>
<body>
Sara,

Below is the memo I circulated on September 19th outlining the September 17th meeting. Check the second bullet in my summary. I recall Manuella wasn’t present that day, but Marcelo actively contributed throughout the discussion.

I couldn’t locate my copy, but luckily Matteo still had his version.
</body>
<quoted>
 -----Original Message-----
From: 	Mendes, Matteo  
Sent:	Monday, December 16, 2024 10:20 AM
To:	Ferreira, Heitor
Subject:	FW: Summary of Meeting on Warehouse Space Reallocation 

FYI

 -----Original Message-----
From: 	Ferreira, Heitor  
Sent:	Thursday, September 19, 2024 2:25 PM
To:	Moraes, Sara; Machado, Manuella; Mendonça, Dom; da Cunha, Heitor; Mendes, Matteo; Câmara, Ryan; Vieira, Luiz Miguel; Novaes, Antônio; Lopes, Arthur Miguel; Oliveira, Pedro; Camargo, Levi; Cassiano, Marcelo; Souza, João Miguel; Cunha, Cecília; Porto, Sophie; Santos, Levi
Cc:	Cunha, Heitor; Campos, Daniel; Correia, Nina
Subject:	Summary of Meeting on Warehouse Space Reallocation 

The following summarizes the outcome of our meeting......If you want to discuss further, please call me.

São Paulo area split by warehouse sector
The decision was made to divide the Field Operations warehouse area into two sectors; São Bernardo and North São Paulo, instead of three sectors or dividing by individual locations. If further subdivisions are necessary later, those changes can be implemented then. Updates to the WMS system are needed. I spoke with Daniel Campos and Heitor Cunha and learned these updates are straightforward and could be completed within a couple of days.
Luiz Miguel Vieira and I will identify which deferred shipment points fall into these new sectors and then pass that information to Daniel and Heitor.

Question: Should we implement this change immediately or hold off until the next logistics cycle?

Shift from 'net zero' scheduling / Ensure minimum activity threshold
This topic was postponed for now. The planned shipment schedule does not always reflect actual fleet movements. Usually, the flexibility provided by Luiz Gustavo Siqueira allows Fleet Operations to adjust routes to maintain minimum delivery levels to the Guarulhos and Itaim warehouses. More analysis is needed. Levi Camargo, Pedro Oliveira and I will keep monitoring system operations to decide if further adjustments are necessary.

Send alert when final scheduled shipments exceed capacity
The IT team will update the scheduling system to add a step comparing the final scheduled shipment volume with warehouse capacity. If the scheduled volume surpasses capacity, I will receive an automatic email alert. This will help track such incidents and assess their impact. I will coordinate with Matteo Mendes to finalize this process.
</quoted>
